# Product intent with Ready Room

A product's intent lives in its repository under product/ as a Ready Intent
Package (RIP): typed `.ready` records, one per file, in the format below.
Ready Room shows the RIP to the person and their team through the Ready Room
connector (the `readyroom` MCP server this plugin adds).

Use this skill when the person asks to create, change, or check the product
intent under product/, or whether the code matches it. Change intent only as
the person directs; code, questions, and your own suggestions are evidence.

## The loop

1. Edit: read product/product.ready, the affected capabilities and the shared
   records they link, then edit the files under product/.
2. Validate: from the repository root, run `npx @readyroom/ready validate .`
   and fix what it reports until it shows 0 errors and 0 warnings.
3. Send: call `send_working_copy` with the project's name, a label for the
   version (such as the branch or worktree), and the model you are running as;
   or pass a repository_id from `list_repositories` to send to it again. It
   returns a command: run it in a shell from the repository root. It uploads
   product/ and prints what Ready Room received. Send again after every change
   under product/.
4. Open the room: call `open_room` with the repository_id to show the person
   the room card.
5. Check: call `start_check` with scope `changed` for what this session
   touched, or `full` when the person asks for a full check. Read the code
   and the RIP on disk yourself, then finish with `report_check`.
6. Ask: when the RIP does not settle something the person must decide, ask
   with `ask_member` (to show an open question, take its question_id from
   `list_questions`). Edit product/ as the answer directs, validate, and send
   again. Close questions with `close_question` only when the person says
   they no longer apply.

If the Ready Room tools are unavailable, the person has not signed in yet: ask
them to run `/mcp`, choose readyroom, and sign in in the browser. Editing and
validating product/ work without Ready Room.

## .ready records

Ready standard 8: a Ready Intent Package (RIP) is a graph of typed records.
This is format guidance, not product behavior or authorization to change intent.
Read product/product.ready, the affected capabilities, their flows and sequences,
and the shared records they reference before editing. Only owner direction
changes intent; repository code, questions and agent suggestions are evidence.

One YAML record per .ready file under product/. Every record has ready: 2,
kind, id; optional common fields are display_id, summary, rationale, notes,
files [{path, title?, role?}], and tags [{tag, text}]. A file path starts with
product/; file roles are contract|prompt|mockup|config|schema|doc|example.
The only kinds are product, capability, flow, step, sequence, entity,
data_group, interface, trigger, rule, actor, system, constant, and term.
Unknown fields are refused. In the field lists below, ? means optional and
[] means a list. Titles and names are per kind. Every summary is one sentence,
at most 160 characters. Write present-tense current intent, never tasks or history.

Ids are unique lowercase dotted names. Behavior ids begin with their capability
(generate.create-font); shared ids begin with their kind (data.fonts,
interface.preview, rule.cost). Keep ids and display ids stable; if one changes,
update every reference and code citation. There are no alternate-name fields.
Display-id prefixes: CAP-, FLOW-, SEQ-, DATA-, IF-, RULE-, TRIG-, ACTOR-, SYS-,
CONST-, TERM-. Cite display_id (or id) in code and tickets.

One home per fact: a capability owns its flows and sequences; a step belongs
to its flow. Rules and triggers have capability only when used in one capability.
Everything else is shared. Consumers link by id instead of repeating behavior.
Folders are convention; fields determine ownership. Suggested paths:
product/product.ready
product/capabilities/<capability>/capability.ready
product/capabilities/<capability>/flows/<flow>.ready
product/capabilities/<capability>/flows/<flow>/<step>.ready
product/capabilities/<capability>/sequences/<sequence>.ready
product/capabilities/<capability>/rules/<rule>.ready
product/capabilities/<capability>/triggers/<trigger>.ready
product/shared/{data,interfaces,actors,systems,triggers,rules,constants,terms}/
product/files/ for referenced supplementary files.

The four forms are data schema (entity, data_group), flow (flow, step),
sequence, and interface. Named actors, systems, triggers, rules, constants and
terms are defined once and referenced from these forms. Layout, overviews,
used-in lists, flow links, sequence start/end steps and entity lifecycles are derived.
A step is a place its subject can be; a sequence is work between steps. The
format assigns no special interruption, compensation or resting-state meaning.

Record fields:

- product: name (at most 40 characters), outcome (at most 300), format_version: 8.0.0, release?, boundary? {text?, includes?[], excludes?[]}, exclusions?[],
  measures?[], dcl? {level: 1..10, basis}, the optional product default.
- capability: name, outcome, actors [actor ids], order?, dcl? {level: 1..10,
  basis}. Each capability is
  an actor's outcome; a CLI, plugin or app channel contributes interfaces.
- flow: capability, title, subject (actor or entity id), steps [ordered step
  ids], entries? [{label, from? (step in another flow), to (step in this flow),
  trigger?}], parts?[], part_of?. An actor subject displays as a journey; an
  entity subject displays as a lifecycle. Both are kind: flow. Links are
  derived: a flow leads to every flow whose entries come from one of its steps.
  A journey moves a lifecycle when an edge of each runs the same sequence or
  one of its steps names a state of that lifecycle in data[].state.
- step: flow, title, step_kind, edges?[], data? [{entity, access: read|write,
  state? (the state-step id in that entity's lifecycle)}], rules?[].
  Journey step_kind: screen|action|decision|system|outcome|error. Optional
  fields: interface (a surface interface id), presentation (screen|inline|
  sheet|dialog|toast|email|notification|external), platforms[], roles[],
  copy {title?, body?[], actions?[], hints?[]}, sees[], does[]. Copy is exact
  quoted user-visible text with {slot} placeholders; sees and does describe.
  Lifecycle step_kind: state; initial?, final?, description?, field?, value?.
  Each edge is {to (step id or $return), trigger (trigger id), guard?, rules?[],
  label?, sequence?, outcome?, channel? (email|push|async|link), platforms?[],
  roles?[]}. Platforms: ios|android|web|mobile|desktop. A guard is plain words.
  Every edge names a trigger. An edge with system work names its sequence and
  one outcome id. All edges running that sequence leave the same step with the
  same trigger, one per outcome; outcome maps to the destination. Pure movement
  needs no sequence. Final steps have no outgoing edges. Never store sequence
  lists on steps or flows: start and end steps are derived from edges.
- sequence: capability, title, participants[], items[], outcomes [{id, label}],
  trigger? (trigger id), parts?[], part_of?. A sequence runs from an edge, an
  invoking message, or its own schedule, event or call trigger. An edge-run
  sequence has no trigger field. Participants are actor, system or interface
  ids, or {id, is? [actor/system/interface ids], label?} lanes. Messages use
  lane ids. A single outcome is reached at the end; an ending alt branch names
  its outcome. Flow edges map outcomes to destination steps.
- interface: interface_kind: surface|operation, name, system?, audience?
  [actor ids], code?. A surface adds surface_kind: app|page|screen|section|
  dialog|sheet|email|notification|provider; parent?, route?, platforms?[],
  elements? [{name, description?, states?[], copy? (text)}], states?[],
  mockup? {url?, file?, frame?, version?}. An operation adds operation_kind:
  endpoint|rpc|mcp_tool|mcp_resource|cli_command|webhook|function; params?
  [{name, type, source}], returns?, errors? [{code, status?, when?, copy?}],
  http? {method, path}, auth?. Never mix the two sets of fields. A step shows
  on a surface via step.interface; a message calls an operation via msg.interface.
- trigger: name, trigger_kind: action|event|schedule|call; capability?, actor?,
  interface? (where it fires), schedule?. Name is the plain-words edge label.
- rule: title, rule_kind: decision|invariant|policy|quality; capability?,
  rules? [other applied rules], constants?[], constraints? [{text, hard?}].
  decision logic: when?/then?/otherwise?, decision? {nodes, edges}, table?
  {columns[], rows[][]}, judge? {evidence[], output, gate?, prompt?}; also
  default?, precedence?[], inputs?[], params? [{name, value, unit?, source?}],
  calculations? [{name, expr, notes?}], sets? [{name, members[]}].
  invariant logic: holds, scope [entity or flow ids].
  policy logic: whenever, then, sequence? (the sequence carrying it out).
  quality logic: applies_to [flow, sequence or interface ids], measure, target,
  scope? (text). Supply logic for the selected kind. Apply decision and policy
  rules from a step, edge, sequence message/note or another applied rule;
  a policy can apply through its sequence. Invariant scope and quality
  applies_to establish their application. No orphan logic.
- entity: table, name, columns[]; entity_kind? (table|view|object|projection|
  external), schema?, primary_key?[], column_groups? [{name, display_id?,
  columns[], summary?}], derivations? [{by, columns[], text}], indexes?[],
  checks? [{name?, expr, purpose?}], coordination? [{id, coordination_kind?
  (lease|lock|admit|fence|other), scope?, owner?, fence?, expires?, limit?,
  protects?, text}], triggers? [{name, timing?, event?, does}], access?
  {rls?, grants?[], readers?[], writers?[]}, view? {source, security_invoker?},
  projection_of?, relationships?[], volume?.
  Columns: {name, type, keys? [PK|FK|UK], fk? {entity, column, on_delete?,
  on_update?}, nullable?, default?, check?, values?[], generated?, visibility?,
  rule?, indexes? [badges], constants?[]}. Indexes: {id (badge), name, purpose,
  display_id?, requested_by? (capability), unique?, method?, columns?[],
  include?[], where?, params?, definition?, serves? [sequence ids]}.
  Relationships: {to (entity), link: fk|logical, label, on? [{from, to}],
  from_card?, to_card?, on_delete?, reason?}; cardinalities are 1, 0..1,
  0..many, 1..many or bounded ranges. The entity's lifecycle is a flow whose
  subject is its id; always-true conditions are invariant rules.
- data_group: title, entities [entity ids], diagram? {nodes, edges}, parts?[],
  part_of?. Groups shared entities in one data diagram.
- actor: name, side: person|operator|agent|third_party|product; description?,
  goal?, connections? [{to, label?, direction? (to|both)}].
- system: name, role; system_kind? (platform|app|service|worker|database|
  storage|queue|external), hosting?, within?, code?, responsibilities?[],
  connections? [{to, label?, direction? (to|both)}], environments? [{name,
  notes?}], units? [{name, unit_kind? (function|job|schedule|service|queue),
  schedule?, resources?, notes?}], secrets? [names only, never values].
- constant: name; value?, unit?, source?, description?, table? {columns[], rows[][]}.
- term: name, definition; synonyms?[], copy_word?.

Sequence items each contain exactly one key:
msg {from, to, text, reply?, interface?, call?, http? {method, path, body?},
auth?, owner?, invokes? [sequence ids], inputs? [{name, source, source_kind?
(surface|parameter|return|stored|payload|session|constant|config|derived)}],
guards?[], ops?[], rules?[], constants?[], results? [{status?, code?, copy?,
when?}], timeout?, retry?, idempotency?, note?, tags?[]};
note {over [lane ids], text, ops?[], rules?[], tags?[]};
alt {branches [{when, outcome?, items[]}]}; opt {when, items[]};
loop {while, max?, items[]}; par {branches [{label?, items[]}]};
break {when, items[]}; transaction {label?, items[]}; continue {to, text?}.
Data operations: {op: read|insert|update|upsert|delete|lock|audit|enqueue|write|
append, entity? (entity or data_group), by?[], index? (entity index badge),
where?, join? [{entity, on}], set?[], conflict?, order?, limit?, mode?, path?,
returns?, triggers?[], shared_with? [sequence ids], note?}. Omit entity only
for a path-addressed object. Rule graph and data diagram nodes: {id,
node_kind: input|decision|calc|judge|action|outcome|data|note, text, ops?[],
refs?[]}; edges: {from, to, label?, undirected?}.

Split flows over 12 steps and sequences over 16 messages into lettered parts:
the overview lists parts; each part names part_of. Keep both directions in sync.
Plain words first: titles, summary, copy, sees, does, guards, labels, trigger
names, message/note/node text describe behavior without identifiers. Put calls
in call, code in code or owner, columns in ops.by/set, results in returns,
record references in refs and constants in constants. Rationale explains why;
notes hold context. Never bury behavior in prose when a typed field fits it.
Keep every fact; when no field fits, use notes, tags or a referenced file, and
raise the missing shape with the owner. Keep unchanged records byte for byte.

Validate the package with the repository's Ready validator before completing
edits. check_rip_changes applies the same validation to an agent's changed_files.
Fix every new error, including record.version (ready must be 2), field.unknown,
ref.missing/ref.kind, home.capability, flow.subject/empty, step.flow/kind,
edge.trigger/sequence/start, sequence.participant, rule.empty/orphan/decision,
interface.fields, and data/schema errors. Review warnings for shared ownership,
unreached sequences, unmapped outcomes, unused interfaces/triggers, data states,
plain words, missing/long summaries and oversized flows/sequences. Maintain all
references, parts, flow steps, sequence outcomes and rule applications together.

Honor the effective DCL; it describes target intent only. A capability uses its
own dcl when set, otherwise the product default, otherwise none. Its basis says
why it differs; dcl.same warns when its level equals the product's. Owned records
use their capability's effective DCL. Shared records have no dcl field: their
effective DCL is the highest among the capabilities that use them, derived from
used-in lookups. Concrete targets such as response time or loss limits belong
in quality rules. At DCL 3, visible failure and owner retry suffice;
authorization, credential secrecy, isolation, money safety and data integrity
still apply. Keep discussion, questions, tasks, research and implementation
notes outside the RIP. Runtime owners in records express intent, not proof
that matching source files exist.
